key_insight: The paper shows that it is often not worth paying for the highest-fidelity LLM or oracle at every step: adaptive switching can achieve similar optimization quality at lower total cost.
engineering_relevance: For data curation and decision pipelines, it provides a principled way to choose when to use expensive high-quality models versus cheaper noisy ones based on downstream optimization value.
method: Cost-aware restarted optimization with adaptive oracle switching when bias is known.
Budgeted certification with occasional trusted-gradient checks to detect and eliminate biased sources when bias is unknown.
Concrete instantiations using biased stochastic gradient extrapolation and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise.
evidence_signal: Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments show the adaptive policy skips several expensive LLM calls while maintaining comparable accuracy and reducing cumulative cost.
watch_item: The certification approach depends on occasional trusted evaluations, so its practical benefit can be reduced if trusted checks are costly or if bias is detected only after substantial delay.
paper_title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
